# Test fixtures

Every image here is either in the public domain or generated by
`scripts/make-fixtures.py`, which is deterministic.

| File | What it is | Source and licence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `scott-kelly.jpg` | Official NASA portrait of astronaut Scott J. Kelly, 27 May 1999. 1280 × 1600 downscale of the 2400 × 3000 original. | [Wikimedia Commons: File:Scott J Kelly.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Scott_J_Kelly.jpg). Photo by NASA; public domain as a work of the US federal government. |
| `mark-kelly.jpg` | Official NASA portrait of astronaut Mark E. Kelly, 5 January 2005. 1280 × 1600 downscale of the 2400 × 3000 original. | [Wikimedia Commons: File:Mark E. Kelly.jpg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Mark_E._Kelly.jpg). Photo by NASA/JSC; public domain as a work of the US federal government. |
| `pattern-a.png` | 1200 × 900 warm gradient with rings and a 60 px grid, for filtering and edge tests. | Generated. |
| `pattern-b.png` | 900 × 1200 cool gradient with a checkerboard and a bright bar. | Generated. |
| `rotated-6.jpg` | 600 × 400 JPEG stored sideways with EXIF orientation 6. It shows an upright "F" only when the orientation is honoured. | Generated (ffmpeg encodes, the script adds the EXIF segment). |
| `p3-red.png` | 320 × 240, left half pure Display P3 red, tagged with the core's own Display P3 ICC profile. That red is outside sRGB. | Generated (the profile comes from `cargo run --example icc -- p3`). |

The Kelly brothers are identical twins, which makes them a good test of
face alignment: the faces match, but the two portraits differ in scale,
position and framing. The same two photos ship as the app's samples in
`web/public/samples`.

Regenerate the synthetic files with:

```sh
python3 scripts/make-fixtures.py
```
